correctness.rationale: Direct bijection classifies every branch as a collapse onto one of L maximal target leaves or as a surjection from its s_i leaves onto a selected target branch of t_j leaves; source root and leaves have forced ranks, and global surjectivity is equivalent to use of all k target intermediate vertices. Stirling inclusion-exclusion counts each local surjection, independent factors count source choices, and inclusion-exclusion on missing target centers gives the total. Full up-set equation is explicitly checked for 50 small profile pairs and an independently coded subset DP agrees on 13,260 pairs; proof handles all positive integer vectors.

value.rationale: The branch-profile count is a natural exact invariant of how many quotient p-morphisms realize a prescribed rooted-tree frame, not a chosen parameter slice: all positive irregular vectors are covered. Unlike the known tree-case Boolean decision algorithm, the polynomial records multiple target-branch usage multiplicities and leaf collapses simultaneously, with quantitative relevance to dual finite Heyting-algebra embeddings and exact quotient counting. It is a structural counting classification, not merely a rewritten feasibility check.
